extra.message: The backup appName from the request body (DeployHistory.appName in DeployController.serverReduction) is concatenated directly into a shell command 'rm -rf ' + deployPath + '/' + resources.getAppName() and executed on the managed server via ExecuteShellUtil. An authenticated user can supply an appName such as 'x; <arbitrary command>' to execute OS commands on the remote host. The same value also flows into the 'cp -r' command on line 372.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command

extra.message: app.getDeployScript() is user-controlled (App.deployScript set through AppController, only the app name is validated against '; | &' in AppServiceImpl) and is passed directly to ExecuteShellUtil.execute(), which runs it in a remote shell. A user with app:edit can store an arbitrary shell payload and trigger remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command

extra.message: app.getStartScript() is stored from the App API without shell metacharacter validation and is executed directly on the remote server via ExecuteShellUtil.execute(). This allows OS command injection / remote code execution through the application start script field.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command

extra.message: genConfig.getTableName() is taken from the /api/generator/{tableName}/{type} path variable (via genConfigService.find(tableName)) and is concatenated into tempPath without sanitization. A tableName containing '../' escapes the intended temp directory, so downloading generated code (type=2) writes files outside the intended location (path traversal / arbitrary file write).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: genConfig.getApiPath() and genConfig.getPath() are attacker-controlled persisted values (GenConfigController.updateGenConfig accepts an arbitrary @RequestBody GenConfig) and are concatenated into the output file path without validation in getFrontFilePath(). An attacker can set path to an absolute/relative traversal path and cause generated front-end files to be written anywhere on disk.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The PUT /api/users/resetPwd endpoint has no @PreAuthorize permission check (unlike every other privileged UserController method). Any authenticated user, regardless of role, can reset the password of any account including the administrator, leading to full account takeover (broken access control).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The DELETE /api/localStorage endpoint has no @PreAuthorize check, unlike query/create/update which require storage permissions. Any authenticated user can delete arbitrary stored files by supplying their IDs; LocalStorageServiceImpl.deleteAll() then removes the underlying files from disk.

PUT /api/aliPay (updateAliPayConfig) has no @PreAuthorize permission check. Any authenticated user can overwrite the Alipay payment gateway/appId/publicKey/privateKey configuration, redirecting payments or breaking payment integrity.

GET /api/aliPay (queryAliConfig) has no @PreAuthorize check and returns the AlipayConfig entity, which includes payment gateway keys and credentials. Any authenticated user can read sensitive payment configuration.

The whole EmailController (GET queryEmailConfig, PUT updateEmailConfig, POST sendEmail) has no @PreAuthorize checks. Any authenticated user can read the mail credentials, reconfigure the SMTP host/account/password, and send arbitrary emails through the server (used for phishing/spam).

None of the /api/generator endpoints (query tables/columns, save column definitions, sync, and generate/preview/download code) has a @PreAuthorize permission check. Any authenticated user can dump database schema metadata and invoke the code generator, which writes files to attacker-influenced paths (see GenUtil path traversal findings).

GenConfigController has no @PreAuthorize checks on GET/PUT /api/genConfig. Any authenticated user can read and modify generator configuration, including the path/moduleName/apiPath values later used to build file system paths, enabling arbitrary file writes via the generator.

POST /api/s3Storage (uploadS3Storage) and GET /api/s3Storage/download/{id} (downloadS3Storage) have no @PreAuthorize checks, unlike the list/delete endpoints. Any authenticated user can upload arbitrary files into the object storage bucket and enumerate/download file metadata by ID.

The password field of UserDto is serialized to JSON (unlike isAdmin, which is annotated @JSONField(serialize = false)). UserDto is returned by GET /api/users (queryUser) and by /auth/info (JwtUserDto.user), exposing BCrypt password hashes of all users to any caller with user:list (and to the user's own session).

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: A hardcoded symmetric encryption key/IV 'Passw0rd' is embedded in EncryptUtils and used for DES encryption of stored secrets such as the email account password. Anyone with the source can decrypt stored credentials. DES with a static key/IV is cryptographically broken (CWE-798/CWE-321/CWE-327).

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: The development datasource configuration hardcodes database credentials (username root / password 123456) directly in the committed configuration file. These default credentials are also the fallback values in the production profile and are widely known, allowing direct database access.

The production Druid stat-view-servlet is enabled and exposes a management console protected by hardcoded default credentials (login-username admin / login-password 123456). Combined with permitAll('/druid/**'), this grants anyone access to the database monitoring console.

The Druid monitoring console path is explicitly permitted to all users (.antMatchers("/druid/**").permitAll()). The console exposes connection pool state, SQL statistics and (in prod) is guarded only by default credentials, constituting an unauthenticated administrative interface exposure.

CORS is configured with setAllowCredentials(true) together with addAllowedOriginPattern("*"), permitting credentialed cross-origin requests from any website. A malicious page can make authenticated requests using the victim's credentials/token, defeating same-origin protections.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The Redis value serializer writes class information (JSONWriter.Feature.WriteClassName) and deserializes with fastjson2 JSON.parseObject after registering an autoType whitelist for the 'me.zhengjie' package. Objects placed into Redis are deserialized polymorphically; if an attacker can write to the Redis cache (or influence cached content), this enables type-confusion/gadget deserialization within the whitelisted package hierarchy (CWE-502).

testConnection() passes a fully user-controlled JDBC URL (POST /api/database/testConnect) to SqlUtils.getConnection/DriverManager, which opens a network connection to the supplied host. sanitizeJdbcUrl only disables a fixed set of parameters; it does not restrict the host, so an authenticated user can force the server to connect to arbitrary internal hosts/ports (SSRF) or trigger JDBC attack vectors.

QuartzRunnable resolves and invokes an arbitrary public method (methodName) on any Spring service bean selected by beanName. QuartzJobController.checkBean() only validates that beanName is a known service bean, not the method, so an authenticated user with timing:add/edit can invoke unintended methods (including dangerous utility methods) on application beans via reflection.

cwe: CWE-470: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code
CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
